findings.body:
`0008_drop_reason` depends on `("billing", "0007_add_reason")`, but this PR deletes `migrations/0007_add_reason.py`. Django cannot build the graph and will raise `NodeNotFoundError: Migration billing.0008_drop_reason dependencies reference nonexistent parent node ('billing', '0007_add_reason')`, so `migrate` fails and the column is never dropped.

Keep `0007_add_reason` in the tree and leave this dependency as-is so `RemoveField` can apply on top of it. If `0007` was never shipped, drop this file too and delete `0007` only.

`RemoveField` on `invoice.void_reason` emits `DROP COLUMN` with no copy/backup step. The comment that the field was never surfaced in the UI does not guarantee the column is empty — a void reason is often written at void time even when it is not rendered.

Once the missing `0007` parent is restored so this migration can run, any stored values are discarded. Confirm no environment has data (or export it first) before applying.

summary:
I'd recommend not merging until the migration graph is repaired: `0008_drop_reason` cannot load because this PR deletes its parent.

`migrations/0008_drop_reason.py` declares `dependencies = [("billing", "0007_add_reason")]`, but `migrations/0007_add_reason.py` is removed in the same commit. Django will raise `NodeNotFoundError` and refuse to migrate, so the column is not dropped and no later `billing` migration can apply.

The usual Django shape for this change is: **keep** `0007_add_reason` (it is already in the chain after `0006_initial`) and add `0008` as a follow-on `RemoveField`. If `0007` has never been applied anywhere, delete `0007` and do not add `0008` at all.

`RemoveField` is still a `DROP COLUMN`. A comment that the field was never shown in the UI does not mean it is empty; confirm no environment stored `void_reason` (or copy the values out) before this runs. This tree has no `Invoice` model or other callers to re-check that claim.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: PR deletes migrations/0007_add_reason.py while new 0008_drop_reason.py still lists dependencies = [("billing", "0007_add_reason")]; at HEAD that parent file is missing, so Django’s migration graph cannot resolve and migrate will fail with NodeNotFoundError.

The new migration runs RemoveField on invoice.void_reason with only a UI comment and no copy/backup operation, so applying it will DROP the column and discard any stored values. Warning severity is appropriate for this irreversible schema change.
